author: Joshua Fluke
description:
Apparently one of the new job interview questions is what you do when it’s 5:00 p.m. on Friday and you still have 20% of your monthly AI subscription left.

My answer?

I go home.

But according to this new version of corporate productivity culture, unused AI tokens are apparently wasted potential.

Employees are becoming “managers of compute,” and leaving Claude Code or other AI capacity unused means you could have been generating more code, running more audits, analyzing more data, building more internal tools or otherwise finding something — anything — to keep the machine busy.

And that’s exactly the problem.

Using more resources does not automatically mean creating more value.

In this video, we’re talking about AI productivity, Claude Code, AI-token usage, employee monitoring, keystroke tracking, mouse tracking, Microsoft Teams status, lines of code, Goodhart’s law and why corporate productivity metrics so often end up measuring activity instead of actual results.
